title: Stitched Value Model for Diffusion Alignment
claim: Existing value estimators are biased or costly; stitching a pretrained reward model onto a noisy-latent backbone is efficient, unbiased and low-variance.
layout: Left: 3 stacked rows (a)-(c), left-to-right; right: zoomed stitching diagram
description: The left side stacks three horizontal pipelines under the heading 'Value Function Approximation'. (a) Tweedie runs z_t through a DiT, a VAE decoder, x_0 and a reward model (RM) to a reward. (b) Monte Carlo runs three parallel k-step denoising rollouts that merge into one reward. (c) StitchVM, the proposed method, is a single compact block that maps z_t straight to a reward. Each row has a checklist of Efficient, Unbiased and Low variance, marked with red ✗ or green ✓ icons. Row (c) is all green. A grey callout on the right expands StitchVM. It shows orange DiT layers cut by scissors, a red stitching layer, then blue RM layers. It is annotated with 'noisy latent space', 'clean pixel space' and the two sources of knowledge. Orange, blue and red color-code the components.
caption: StitchVM overview. Left: Unlike Tweedie (a), which requires a denoiser and VAE decoder evaluations and is biased in high noise, and MC (b), which requires N-denoising rollouts, StitchVM (c) directly evaluates the value function on noisy latents. Right: StitchVM stitches a diffusion backbone head to a reward model tail, turning the reward model into a value model.
abstract: Reward-based alignment of diffusion and flow models requires estimating the value function at noisy intermediate latents, although pretrained reward models operate on clean images. Common approaches use Tweedie-style clean-image proxies or Monte Carlo rollouts, introducing approximation bias or substantial computational cost. Directly learning the value function offers an alternative, but matching the performance and generalization of foundation-scale pixel-space reward models on noisy latents remains challenging. We address this gap by transferring pretrained reward capabilities to noisy latents. We propose \textbf{StitchVM} (Stitched Value Model), a model stitching framework that connects a frozen diffusion-backbone prefix to a pretrained reward-model suffix through a compatible feature interface. A closed-form feature fit selects the interface, and lightweight distillation adapts the stitched model, combining noise-aware diffusion features with pretrained reward capability. For example, adapting CLIP ViT-L with SD~3.5 Medium at $512\times512$ resolution takes approximately 10 GPU-hours on a single GH200. Once trained, StitchVM provides an amortized alternative to Tweedie-style and Monte Carlo approximations of the value function: it estimates value directly from noisy latents, avoiding clean-image reconstruction and additional denoising rollouts for each evaluation. We demonstrate benefits across inference-time steering and post-training. StitchVM improves the quality and efficiency of FK steering and DRaFT, accelerates DPS by $3.7\times$ with half the peak GPU memory, and accelerates DiffusionNFT by $2.3\times$.
